records.title: PointDetector: Large-Scale Lithography Hotspot Detection via Point Cloud Classification
records.summary: Lithography hotspot detection is essential for ensuring yield and reliability in integrated circuit manufacturing. However, existing approaches typically analyze small layout clips in isolation, resulting in inefficient and fragmented detection workflows. In this work, we propose a novel formulation of hotspot detection as a point cloud classification problem and introduce a tailored neural network architecture based on submanifold sparse convolution to efficiently process large layouts. Our method operates directly on polygon segments used in mask optimization, enabling fine-grained predictions aligned with downstream hotspot fixing. By representing layouts as point clouds and leveraging the sparsity of the data, our approach supports large-scale detection with a single forward pass, improving runtime over the compared clip-based methods. Experimental results on large benchmark datasets show that our method achieves up to 20 × faster inference than existing detection-based techniques while also improving precision, recall, F1 score, and false alarms by 30.0%, 59.6%, 46.0%, and 80.8%, respectively, on our large-scale benchmark. These results highlight the potential of our approach to enable fast, scalable, and fine-grained hotspot detection for advanced IC manufacturing.

records.title: HaVen-Agent: Enhancing Hallucination-Mitigated Verilog Code Generation Aligned with HDL Engineers through Code Repair and Multi-Agent Orchestration
records.summary: Recently, the use of large language models (LLMs) for Verilog code generation has attracted great research interest to enable hardware design automation. However, previous works have shown a gap between the ability of LLMs and the practical demands of hardware description language (HDL) engineering. This gap includes differences in how engineers phrase questions and hallucinations in the generated code. To address these challenges, we introduce HaVen , a novel LLM framework designed to mitigate hallucinations and align Verilog code generation with the practices of HDL engineers. HaVen tackles hallucination issues by proposing a comprehensive taxonomy and employing a chain-of-thought (CoT) mechanism to translate symbolic modalities ( e .g. truth tables, state diagrams, e tc.) into accurate natural language descriptions. Furthermore, HaVen bridges this gap by using a data augmentation strategy, synthesizing high-quality instruction-code pairs that match real HDL engineering practices. Building upon HaVen , we develop HaVen -R, a reasoning-augmented extension fine-tuned with a Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RFT) Dataset and a Reasoning Dataset, enabling Chain-of-Thought (CoT) guided self-reflection to iteratively repair Verilog code. We further introduce HaVen -Agent, a multi-agent system that orchestrates a Planner Agent (GPT-4o), a Coder Agent ( HaVen -R), and a Verifier Agent for iterative code repair. Our experiments demonstrate that HaVen -Agent significantly improves the correctness of Verilog code generation, outperforming state-of-the-art methods on VerilogEval and RTLLM benchmarks. Additional evaluations include a 400-case multi-generator repair study, component and iteration ablations, CVDP, end-to-end cost and latency analysis, and protocol-aware comparisons with recent feedback, agentic, and reasoning-augmented methods. HaVen is publicly available at https://github.com/Intelligent-Computing-Research-Group/HaVen.

records.title: AutoShrink 2.0: Automating Large-Scale Pareto Optimization in HLS via Adaptive and Cost-Aware Search Space Shrinkage
records.summary: High-level synthesis (HLS) expedites accelerator customization by delivering a high-level hardware programming paradigm and offering a rich set of optimization directives. However, the quality of HLS designs is highly dependent on the designers’ selection of directives in the trade-off between different design metrics, which is non-trivial and can lead to a large design turnaround time. Design space exploration (DSE) serves as a promising solution to this problem, but existing studies on DSE suffer from a lack of scalability for large-scale applications and often spend a substantial portion of the exploration budget on costly design points. To address this problem, this paper proposes AutoShrink 2.0 , a DSE engine that adaptively shrinks the large search space of an HLS design to gradually retain only high-quality solutions. AutoShrink 2.0 incorporates (1) a comprehensive design space pruning strategy that integrates the joint effect of directives and domain knowledge, (2) an importance-guided Pareto optimization algorithm which dynamically traces the importance ranking of the applied directives and leverages this ranking to navigate the search direction of Pareto frontiers, and (3) a cost-aware post-filtering mechanism to screen out candidates that are computationally expensive yet of limited gain, reducing runtime overhead within a single evaluation. Experimental results on Vitis HLS demonstrate that AutoShrink 2.0 achieves an average distance to reference set (ADRS) of 8.40% across multiple applications with design spaces containing up to \(\text{10}^\text{16} \) design points, outperforming three heuristic methods and three state-of-the-art approaches by 8.01 × and 6.24 ×, respectively. On timeout-prone benchmarks, the cost-aware post-filtering strategy reduces the average timeout ratio by 66.1% compared with the variant without this strategy. Furthermore, design tool transfer experiments from Vitis HLS to Catapult HLS demonstrate the promising cross-tool applicability of AutoShrink 2.0.

records.title: Provably Correct and Scalable Clock Modeling for FPGA-based Emulation
records.summary: Field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based emulation delivers orders of magnitude higher throughput than software simulation. However, fundamental clocking differences between application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) and FPGAs limit its performance and capacity. To address this, we model the sampling of all flip-flops (FFs), originally triggered by multiple generated clocks, as an ordered sequence of events and reproduce their behavior at each emulation step. We introduce two clock models. The output-gated model (M o ) samples the clock, input, and output of each FF, requiring more logic resources but no event ordering. Conversely, the sampling-gated model (M s ) uses clock edge detection to conditionally sample, using fewer logic resources but requiring event ordering. We then adopt a hybrid strategy that applies M o to clock-generation logic to avoid resolving complex clock dependencies, and applies M s to the data path to save logic resources. We formally prove that the transformed design is sequentially equivalent to the original at every emulation step. We propose matching-point inductive verification (MPIV), which augments the inductive proof with matching points recorded during the transformation and reduces verification tasks to satisfiability (SAT) checks. Across industrial designs with up to 11,515 generated clocks, the hybrid approach incurs modest overhead (1.7% FFs and 5.8% lookup tables (LUTs) on average). MPIV achieves up to 2,950 × speedup and succeeds on large designs where a widely used model checker ABC-PDR times out. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first publicly documented and formally verified methodology for eliminating logic-generated clocks in ASIC-to-FPGA emulation.

records.title: The Deception of Sight: Camouflaging Chips Information Against Optical Probing Attacks By Selective Increase of Local Density
records.summary: In recent years, a novel non-invasive laser-assisted attack known as Optical Probing (OP) has been demonstrated to effectively probe the internal state of integrated circuits. This attack exploits the relative transparency of the silicon substrate to Near-InfraRed (NIR) light, enabling optical access through the backside of the chip. Consequently, OP poses a significant threat to information processed or stored on the chip and may facilitate Intellectual Property (IP) theft or reverse engineering. Existing mitigation techniques can be broadly classified into three categories: (1) fabrication-level modifications, (2) sensor-based countermeasures, and (3) circuit-level design techniques. Fabrication-based countermeasures are costly and often incompatible with standard industrial manufacturing processes, limiting their practicality for OP-resilient chip design. Sensor-based countermeasures may be circumvented by adaptive attackers, whereas circuit-level techniques typically require modifications to the layout of standard-cell libraries. Such modifications are time-consuming and can introduce considerable PPA overheads relative to conventional standard-cell designs. Therefore, this study investigates whether increasing the local layout density around a target logic cell can enhance resilience against OP attacks without requiring modifications beyond the layout level. In this context, local density refers to the fraction of a predefined region surrounding the target cell that is occupied by neighboring logic cells and associated layout structures. Our methodology employs standard logic cells to protect the chip’s sensitive information from an adversary equipped with OP capabilities. We found that increasing the local density of surrounding logic cells near a target logic cell enhances overall reflection, effectively masking the reflection from the target logic cell. This can significantly improve the concealment of the secure cell’s information from the OP attack since the reflections from the neighboring logic cells overlap with the target logic cells that need to be secured. Hence, an adversary cannot distinguish the exact location of the source of reflection. We demonstrate that this methodology can effectively countermeasure against OP attacks by conducting detailed experiments on the relationship between density and reflection, using NAND, INVERTER, NOR, and Flip-Flop cells. We exhaustively evaluated thousands of placement strategies with varying densities to show the efficacy of our technique against OP attacks. Moreover, we demonstrate the integration of our OP attack mitigation technique into the ASIC flow for designing an AES-128 core. We demonstrate that our technique in the worst-case comes with a 1% increase in power consumption, a 1% increase in area, and no change in the operating frequency compared to the unprotected AES-128 core against OP attack.

records.title: Design-Space Exploration for Runtime-Reconfigurable FPGA-Based DNN Accelerators
records.summary: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have recently achieved major gains across many domains, increasing the need for hardware accelerators that can adapt to changing workloads. Because DNN layers have diverse characteristics, each may benefit from a different hardware architecture. FPGAs support this through runtime reconfiguration, but applying it to neural network accelerators remains limited. Reconfiguring the FPGA between every pair of layers would tailor hardware to each layer but incur prohibitive reconfiguration overhead. We address this by proposing a cluster-based approach that groups layers with similar computational requirements and assigns each group a shared hardware configuration. This reduces the number of reconfigurations while preserving efficient execution. However, selecting good clusters and configurations creates a large design space, especially for large networks: too few clusters merges dissimilar layers and hurts efficiency, while too many clusters increases reconfiguration overhead. To tackle this, we present a Design-Space Exploration (DSE) framework that co-optimizes clustering schemes and hardware configurations using genetic algorithms. Our method explores clustering schemes without accuracy loss, as the network and numeric precision remain fixed. Unlike prior work that optimizes only hardware or only mapping, our approach jointly optimizes both. We show that reconfiguring at carefully chosen points reduces overall inference latency despite reconfiguration costs. On GPT-2, ResNet-18, VGG01, VGG02, and AlexNet, our cluster-based designs reduce latency by 20–43% versus a fixed architecture and outperform the Simba and Eyeriss accelerators on four of five models while matching performance on VGG02.

records.title: Constraint-aware HLS optimization via LLM-based multi-role agent with iterative reflexion
records.summary: High-Level Synthesis (HLS) design productivity is often constrained by manual, expert-driven pragma tuning and the difficulty of balancing performance optimization with strict hardware resource limits. While automated Design Space Exploration (DSE) has been extensively studied, many existing approaches rely on open-loop estimation models or substantial training data, which can lead to physically unrealizable designs under tight resource budgets. In this work, we propose Reflex-HLS , a training-free agentic framework that formulates HLS optimization as a closed-loop, feedback-driven process grounded in physical synthesis outcomes. Reflex-HLS integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) within a Planner–Actor–Critic architecture, where optimization decisions are iteratively refined based on hardware-in-the-loop feedback from the vendor toolchain, ensuring physical realizability throughout the optimization process. Experimental results on PolyBench and MachSuite benchmarks, validated through full Vivado synthesis and implementation, demonstrate that Reflex-HLS achieves speedups of up to 48.41 × (e.g., on jacobi-2d ) while strictly adhering to device resource constraints. Further evaluations across regular, irregular, and structured workloads show that the proposed framework generalizes beyond conventional compute kernels. Comparative studies against representative open-loop DSE methods, large foundation models operating without hardware feedback, and closed-loop heuristic search highlight the trade-offs among optimization paradigms, with Reflex-HLS producing more deployable and resource-efficient designs under tight resource budgets in the evaluated cases.

records.title: CGLLR: Classification-based Graded LLR Quantization Scheme for 3D TLC NAND Flash
records.summary: low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes are extensively utilized in triple-level cell (TLC) NAND flash memory due to their robust data error correction capability, with their performance dependent on the decoder’s iterative computation of the Log-Likelihood Ratio (LLR) messages transmitted by the NAND flash memory channel. However, implementing LDPC decoding algorithms in hardware necessitates the quantization of LLR messages due to limited hardware resources, which inevitably diminishes LLR accuracy and subsequently affects LDPC decoding performance. To mitigate this issue, we propose a classification-based graded LLR Quantization Scheme for 3D TLC NAND Flash, termed CGLLR. By employing the k-means clustering algorithm to categorize the quantized initial LLR messages from the channel, we apply distinct quantization factors to different categories of LLR values while preserving the relative magnitudes among the original LLR. This CGLLR strategy significantly enhances the resolution of LLR messages, thereby improving decoding performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed CGLLR scheme reduces the average number of decoding iterations by 26.3% compared to the standard algorithm.

records.title: AceTherm: Accelerated Thermal Analysis of Chiplet Integration Using Non-Conformal FEM
records.summary: As advanced process nodes continue to scale, heterogeneous integration technologies such as 2.5D/3D packaging, chiplets, and high-bandwidth memory have been widely adopted. However, these advances introduce substantially higher power densities, more complex interconnection structures, and increasingly diverse material systems. The resulting localized hotspots raise reliability concerns such as electromigration, thermomechanical stress, and structural warpage, making layout-driven thermal simulation with balanced accuracy and efficiency essential for rapid design iterations. This paper proposes AceTherm, an automated thermal simulation framework driven by Graphic Data System (GDS) layout and Process Design Kit (PDK) process parameters, which integrates non-conformal finite element method with customized sparse-matrix solvers. By exploiting the layered structure of the chip architecture, the simulation domain is sampled and discretized with a non-conformal mesh and high-resolution material mapping, significantly reducing degrees of freedom (DOFs) while preserving accuracy. The mesh division and sampling resolution provide a two-level control for trading off accuracy and speed, and the convergence and error behavior are analyzed to characterize the discrete scheme of AceTherm. Exploiting the structural properties of the resulting coefficient matrix, AceTherm employs supernodal sparse Cholesky factorization to accelerate the solution process. Notably, the symbolic factorization can be reused across multiple thermal load scenarios when the mesh pattern remains unchanged. Numerical experiments show that the proposed method achieves a 104.6 × speedup over the conventional COMSOL solution and reaches up to 539.2 × in repeated or preset-parameter simulations, while maintaining the average temperature error below 1 K. The combination of high computational speed, layer-aware modeling, and sub-Kelvin accuracy positions AceTherm as a practical tool for thermal analysis and optimization in heterogeneous IC back-end design.

records.title: A Delay-Aware Verilog-A Modeling and Simulation Framework for Passive Photonic Integrated Circuits
records.summary: Transmission delays are inherent in silicon photonic integrated circuits (PICs) and have a significant impact on their dynamic behavior and system-level performance. However, conventional modeling and simulation approaches often overlook or inadequately account for these delays, limiting accuracy and efficiency in circuit-level analysis. This paper presents a delay-aware macromodeling methodology that explicitly extracts time delays from frequency-domain responses and incorporates them into a compact pole-residue representation. In contrast to traditional techniques such as complex vector fitting (CVF), which approximate delay effects indirectly and often require a large number of poles, resulting in increased model complexity, reduced simulation efficiency, and potential causality violations, the proposed method captures delays explicitly and compactly without compromising accuracy or physical consistency. To enable integration into circuit simulation workflows, we introduce an efficient Verilog-A implementation of the proposed model, along with practical strategies for representing time delays within standard electronic-photonic co-simulation environments. The proposed approach is validated using three categories of passive PIC structures: waveguides, feedforward multi-path circuits, and resonant (loop-based) circuits, demonstrating superior compactness, simulation speed, and accuracy compared to conventional modeling techniques. These results highlight the method’s potential for scalable and high-fidelity modeling of PICs in hybrid electronic-photonic circuit and system design.

records.title: CLCAD: Cross-Layer Collaborative Anomaly Detection for Continuous-Flow Microfluidic Biochips
records.summary: Continuous-flow microfluidic biochips are widely used in biochemical applications because of their precise control, high integration, and automation. During bioassay execution, the control layer applies pneumatic signals to valves according to the valve activation sequence, ensuring reliable execution in the flow layer. However, in an insecure supply chain, attackers can induce anomalous valve states through Trojan insertion or other malicious means, causing anomalous execution. For example, attackers can tamper with the valve activation sequence of the flow layer or the design scheme of the control layer, thereby causing incorrect valve activation or disrupting control signal delivery to the target valves, respectively. To detect anomalies during execution, we propose CLCAD, a cross-layer collaborative anomaly detection method that collaboratively identifies anomalies in valve states caused by potential attacks in both the flow and control layers. To address tampering with the valve activation sequence, we propose a weight calculation strategy based on fluid scheduling and a checkpoint selection strategy based on discrete particle swarm optimization, enabling checkpoint configuration optimization and detection capability improvement under limited detection resources. To address tampering with the control layer design scheme, we propose a valve addressing scheme detection strategy, a valve synchronization requirement detection strategy, and a test pattern selection strategy based on discrete social learning particle swarm optimization, enabling the selected test patterns to cover a wider range of anomalous behaviors. Experimental results demonstrate that CLCAD effectively improves anomaly detection probability and return on investment while maintaining low detection cost across multiple benchmarks.

records.title: REUSE: Recurrent Subgraph Exploitation for ReRAM-Accelerated Graph Processing
records.summary: Graph accelerators have emerged as a promising solution for accelerating the processing of large-scale sparse graphs by leveraging the in-situ computation capabilities of ReRAM crossbars. However, existing designs incur substantial memristor access overhead due to the large number of graph partitions, increasing execution time and energy consumption while reducing circuit lifetime. This paper presents REUSE, a ReRAM-based graph accelerator that exploits recurring subgraph patterns to minimize memristor write operations. REUSE identifies frequent patterns and maps them to static graph engines whose crossbar configurations are preserved throughout execution, while less frequent patterns are assigned to dynamic engines at runtime. To support efficient mapping, REUSE employs a lightweight host-side processing scheme that operates directly on the graph's coordinate list, avoiding costly dense matrix reconstruction. Patterns are then distributed across multiple crossbars within each graph engine to balance the workload and maximize utilization. Furthermore, we develop analytical execution-time and energy models and use them to explore key architectural parameters, including the allocation of static and dynamic graph engines. REUSE is evaluated on diverse real-world graph datasets using BFS, SSSP, and PageRank, with BFS as the common workload for comparison against four state-of-the-art ReRAM-based accelerators. It achieves average speedups of 6.9 × over SparseMEM, 4.2 × over RPBFS, and 2.5 × over TARe, and improves on GraphR by 76 ×. The corresponding energy-delay product reductions are 7.5 ×, 70 ×, and 4.9 × against the same three designs, and approximately five orders of magnitude against GraphR. Circuit lifetime is extended by 2 × over SparseMEM and by two orders of magnitude over GraphR.

records.title: Best Match: Enhanced Hybrid-Row-Height Standard Cell Placement with Macro Blockages
records.summary: Hybrid-row-height IC design incorporates placement rows of two or more distinct heights which do not have to be integer multiples of a single height. This design strategy is more flexible for optimizing power, performance, and area simultaneously. Several attempts have been made to deal with the hybrid-row-height standard cell placement problem with customizable row configuration by intelligently leveraging a commercial placement tool. Here we propose an enhanced algorithm, Best Match, to determine the best matching row configuration for a given netlist which leads to minimal disturbance to the initial timing-optimized placement after placement legalization. Our row planning approach has a number of enhancements over previous works, including (1) consideration of horizontal displacement of cells in addition to vertical displacement of cells, (2) precise positioning of the hybrid rows, and (3) ability to handle macros in a design. As a result, we obtained a much smaller total displacement of cells after placement legalization compared to the state-of-the-art works. The experimental results show that our approach outperforms the flow-based method in [9] with 48.4%, 24.9%, and 68.8% reduction in the total displacement of cells, final routed wirelength, and post-route total negative slack, respectively. It yielded 13.4% reduction in the total displacement of cells, 4.5% reduction in the final routed wirelength, and 26.3% reduction in the post-route total negative slack compared to [7]. Furthermore, compared to the legalized placement generated by a commercial tool under the uniformly hybrid row configuration, the routed wirelength and post-route total negative slack are reduced by 27.4% and 91.8%, respectively, under the customized row configuration determined by Best Match.

records.title: CAMEO: Compressive Energy-Aware Multi-Task Deep Inference in Resource-Constrained Energy Harvesting Systems
records.summary: Multi-task Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) inference on Energy Harvesting (EH) devices has received limited attention, particularly in scenarios where energy availability fluctuates significantly. This poses substantial implementation challenges, especially in deploying and running inference under varying energy conditions while performing multiple correlated tasks. In this work, we present an end-to-end framework that enables multi-task inference to inherently conserve computation under dynamic energy conditions. To facilitate this adaptation in multi-task settings, we propose inter-task and intra-task shared-weight design strategies. The inter-task design removes redundancy across related tasks, while the intra-task design targets redundancy within weight matrices. Finally, to enable efficient inference on resource-constrained devices, we compress the model and propose novel algorithms that support energy-aware adaptation and compression-tolerant computation without expensive weight reconstruction. Experimental results show that our proposed framework can enable up to 1.8x inference latency reduction, 48% energy efficiency improvement, and 3.5x memory conservation.

records.title: SSRESF-OPT: A Sensitivity-Aware Framework for Single-Particle Radiation Effects Simulation and Optimization in SoC Platforms Using Machine Learning
records.summary: The increasing scale of System-on-Chip (SoC) architectures exacerbates the reliability risks of single-particle radiation effects, rendering traditional exhaustive gate-level fault injection prohibitively slow. To address this, we propose SSRESF-OPT, an end-to-end simulation and optimization framework combining accelerated dynamic fault injection with machine learning-driven prediction. The framework first introduces a cross-layer static binding mechanism to eliminate runtime string resolution, reducing per-injection simulation overhead to \(\mathcal {O}(1) \) complexity. Building on this optimized engine, an SVM-based classification pipeline, guided by structural clustering, accurately predicts the radiation vulnerability of unsimulated circuit nodes using netlist-derived features. To maximize resource efficiency, an OPT-based top- k hardening strategy is then employed to prioritize critical architectural bottlenecks. Evaluations across 15 gate-level netlists, including massive AES subsystems and RISC-V PULP SoCs, demonstrate the framework’s efficacy. The model-assisted approach achieves an average end-to-end runtime speedup of 6.35 × over the highly optimized simulation baseline while maintaining a 94.58% prediction accuracy. Furthermore, hardening only the top 10% of ranked nodes reduces system Soft Error Rate (SER) by 85%, providing a fast and actionable methodology for radiation-hardened microprocessor design.
